attempts.label: CRCNS:cb-1
attempts.entry_title: Interpositus nucleus activity during eyeblink conditioning (ten Brinke et al. 2017)
attempts.summary: The paper's central link held in this data: interpositus facilitation during the CS-US interval tracks eyelid closure trial by trial in both datasets, and spikes lead the eyelid, though by other lags than reported. The counts of facilitating and suppressed cells did not reproduce (80 facilitating cells against the paper's 60), as the classification rests on a criterion the paper does not name. Suppression led the eyelid in both datasets, where the paper reports no lead. CS pauses, US peaks and pauses and their decline with training mostly held in direction, often with counts out of range. The optogenetic inhibition, the Purkinje cell model and the US-only trials could not be tested, as their data are not deposited.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of ten Brinke, Heiney, Wang, Proietti-Onori, Boele, Bakermans, Medina, Gao and De Zeeuw (2017) on CRCNS cb-1, which holds 372 interpositus nucleus recordings with per-trial eyelid and spike traces from two datasets, one recorded over eyeblink conditioning and one after it. It tests the classification of CS-US facilitation and suppression, their relation to conditioned eyelid behavior, the CS pauses and peaks, and the responses to the US. Recording depth is taken from the paper's Source data 1 on eLife, which gives it for the first dataset only. The US-only trials, the optogenetic sessions and the Purkinje cell data are not in the data set.

notebooks.title: Reproducing ten Brinke et al. (2017) from CRCNS cb-1

outcomes.statement: The cells of the paper's Source data 1 are the cells of CRCNS cb-1 in the same order, so that the recording depth Source data 1 gives can be attached to the data set's cells.
outcomes.source: Additional files, Source data 1
outcomes.quote: The two IpN datasets central to this study are combined, with the first 270 cells denoting the first dataset, and the remaining 102 cells denoting the second dataset.
outcomes.notes: Added after the reader's answer (questions/brinke-2017.yaml), which made four claims take recording depth from Source data 1. Matched by order, all 372 cells agree on the number of trials, the per-trial eyelid closure at US onset ('CR @ US ms' equals crAmplitude) and the per-trial baseline rate ('Baseline Hz' equals the spike count over 500 ms, or 200 ms in the second dataset), and Source data 1's 'Cell' is each cell's position; shifted by one cell, 9 of 371 agree on the trial count and none on the other two. Source data 1 gives one depth per cell for the 270 first-dataset cells (1500 to 3000 um) and none for the 102 second-dataset cells.

outcomes.statement: In the first dataset the IpN firing frequency averaged 67 +/- 27 Hz and did not vary with recording depth (r = 0.085, p = 0.16, n = 270, Pearson).
outcomes.source: Results, Characterization of cerebellar IpN neurons, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Firing frequency was similar along the depth of the IpN (r = 0.085, p=0.16, n = 270, Pearson), averaging 67 ± 27 Hz.
outcomes.notes: The reader's answer (questions/brinke-2017.yaml) made the claim data with_inputs, with recording depth from the paper's Source data 1; the earlier run blocked it as data_missing. Under reading (a), the 500 ms baseline, the 270 first-dataset cells fire at 68.3 +/- 26.4 Hz (within 67 +/- 6.7) and the rate does not correlate with depth (Pearson r = 0.086, p = 0.16; the paper's r = 0.085, p = 0.16). Under reading (b), the whole trial, the mean is 70.6 +/- 27.4 Hz and the correlation is significant (r = 0.146, p = 0.0167), so the claim holds under reading (a) only. Within the 11 mice with at least 10 cells no reading (a) correlation is significant (p >= 0.14). The data set's per-trial baseline rates equal Source data 1's 'Baseline Hz' in every cell (source-data-1-link), so the rate side matches the paper's own values.

outcomes.notes: No reading puts all three counts within tolerance. Under the claims file's readings, (a) gives 80 facilitation, 23 suppression and 167 unmodulated cells (only suppression within tolerance) and (b) gives 88 (89 with facilitation first), 31 (30) and 151 (none within tolerance). The cross-correlation estimator is not given in the paper ('temporal cross-correlations between average spike and eyelid traces', Results, IpN facilitation but not suppression can drive conditioned eyelid behavior, paragraph 1). Assumed: the cross-covariance of the two mean-subtracted average traces over the segment, normalized by their norms (MATLAB's xcov with 'coeff'), the standard estimator for two traces. The first round used the Pearson r of the spike segment with the eyelid trace re-cut at each lag, which the verifier found nearly flat across lags on ramp-shaped traces; it is shown as a variant and gives the same outcomes.

findings.statement: The data set holds no recording depth, which the paper uses in four of its findings (Figures 4-figure supplement 1E, 5E, 5J and 6G, and the depth correlation of firing rate). The paper's Source data 1 on the eLife site gives it for the 270 first-dataset cells, which match the data set's cells in order, and for none of the 102 second-dataset cells.

The US-only trials interspersed in 25 second-dataset recordings (Figure 7 and its supplement 1) and the optogenetic sessions of three L7cre-Ai27 mice (Figure 3) are not in the data set; nothing in it marks a trial's type.

The per-trial crAmplitude is described as the eyelid closure at US onset, but it equals the eyelid position 13 ms before the stated US onset (usOnset): exactly in the second dataset (largest difference per recording at most 0.11% closure), and with a median per-recording largest difference of 1.1% closure in the first. At the stated US onset the differences are 5.3 and 13.5% (medians). The second-dataset mean of crAmplitude is the paper's 43.5 +/- 17%.

The per-trial facilitation variable is described only as facilitation during the CS-US interval after subtracting spontaneous facilitation in the baseline. In the second dataset it equals the mean of the positive part of the trial's spike density above the trial's own baseline mean over the whole CS-US interval (0-212 ms), minus the same quantity over the 200 ms baseline. In the first dataset neither the last 200 ms nor the whole interval reproduces it exactly (median per-recording largest difference 4.5 and 8.9 Hz), so its definition there is not documented.

The stored ephysMean is not the mean of the stored ephys trials in 26 recordings (median absolute difference above 1 Hz; largest single difference 158 Hz), while eyelidMean equals the mean of the eyelid trials everywhere.

282 of the 13027 deposited trials have a baseline eyelid at or past half closure, and a Grubbs test on baseline SDs flags 402, while the Methods say such trials were removed. Source data 1 lists exactly the deposited trials as each cell's valid trials, so the trials the paper analysed include them; neither the data set nor the paper says how the exclusions were applied.
The first dataset has 18 mouse IDs (1 to 19 without 10), where the paper's Results say 19 mice and its Methods 22. The second dataset has 6, as the Methods say.
The second dataset's CS-US interval is 212 ms in the data set (usOnset 0.212 s) and its description, but 200 ms in the paper's Results.

paper_notes.statement: The paper's Source data 1 gives Depth as NaN for all 102 second-dataset cells, although Figure 5J reports their depths (2350 +/- 140 against 2450 +/- 211 um), so the second-dataset depths are not public.

Questions for the paper's authors, as no analysis code is linked. (1) How is the 'mean above-baseline activity within the baseline itself' formed for the CS-US modulation classes: the mean of max(baseline - mean, 0) over all baseline bins, the mean over the above-baseline bins only, or the positive parts in both window and baseline (the data set's facilitation variable)? None of these gives 60, 23 and 187 cells here (80/23/167, 62/13/195, 88/31/151), and the authors' own per-cell values in Source data 1 give 84 and 34 cells at 5 Hz; what further criterion selects the 60 and 23? (2) For the CS pause, is 4.5 SDs measured from the baseline mean or as the size of the drop, is the 2 SD rebound measured from the trough or from the baseline, and must the rebound fall within 50-125 ms? (3) How were the 500 random datasets of the bootstrap made? (4) Which normality test decides between Pearson and Spearman? (5) Over which segment and lag range, and with which estimator, were the spike-eyelid cross-correlations taken? With a Pearson r recomputed at each lag many lags sit at the edge of a +/-100 ms range; with the cross-covariance of the two traces at most one does. (6) How is spike rate velocity computed? The first difference of the 1 ms spike density gives two to four times the paper's values. The paper's Source data 1 holds per-cell values that would let these be checked.
The paper gives 19 mice for the first dataset in the Results and n = 25 in all, with 22 for the first and 6 for the second dataset, in the Methods; these do not add up.

The paper's Source data 1 gives each first-dataset cell's mean facilitation and suppression ('Mean Facil Hz', 'Mean Supp Hz'), and 84 and 34 cells reach the stated 5 Hz threshold, where the Results give 60 facilitation and 23 suppression cells. Its undocumented 'Mean US-Cluster' code, read as neither (0), peak only (1, 4), both (2, 3) and pause only (6), gives the Figure 6B counts exactly (31, 134, 77, 28).

entries.title: Interpositus nucleus activity during eyeblink conditioning (ten Brinke et al. 2017)
entries.description: Tests the findings of ten Brinke, Heiney, Wang, Proietti-Onori, Boele, Bakermans, Medina, Gao and De Zeeuw (2017) on CRCNS cb-1, which holds 372 interpositus nucleus recordings with per-trial eyelid and spike traces from two datasets, one recorded over eyeblink conditioning and one after it. It tests the classification of CS-US facilitation and suppression, their relation to conditioned eyelid behavior, the CS pauses and peaks, and the responses to the US. Recording depth is taken from the paper's Source data 1 on eLife, which gives it for the first dataset only. The US-only trials, the optogenetic sessions and the Purkinje cell data are not in the data set.
